cards.explanation: The answer is the ark of God. Verse 2 says they set out “…to bring up from there the ark of God…” So thirty thousand men are heading out for one errand. I once needed a whole afternoon just to move a cooling rack.

The answer is celebrating with all kinds of instruments. Verse 5 says David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of wood instruments, harps, stringed instruments, tambourines, sistrums and cymbals. That's a full band on the road, friends. I can't even get my mixer and my timer to keep the same beat.

The answer is the ark. Verse 6 says Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God, because the oxen had stumbled. This is where the story turns, and I think it's a heavy part. Let's take the next verse slowly.

The answer is that God strikes him down on the spot. Verse 7 says the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down on the spot. He died there beside the ark of God. Uzzah was one of the sons of Abinadab who were guiding the new cart (verse 3).

The answer is irreverence. Verse 7 says God struck Uzzah down on the spot for his irreverence. That's the word the text gives for it. Verse 6 tells us what Uzzah did: he reached out and took hold of the ark of God.

The answer is True. Verse 8 says David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. Then he named the place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day. Verse 9 adds that David feared the LORD that day.

The answer is False. Verse 10 says David was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David. Instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. Obed-edom's house is where the ark goes.

The answer is that the LORD blesses him and his household. Verse 11 says the ark stayed in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed him and all his household. Obed-edom the Gittite is the man who took it in. Three months, friends, and the news is a blessing.

The answer is that David brings the ark up into the City of David. Verse 12 says David went and had the ark of God brought up from the house of Obed-edom into the City of David with rejoicing. The report comes in and David is OUT THE DOOR. I'd have beaten him there if my base had wheels!

The answer is False. Verse 13 speaks of those carrying the ark of the LORD, and no cart is mentioned there. So the ark is carried, friends, not rolled along. When those carrying it had advanced six paces, David sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.

The answer is that David dances with all his might. Verse 14 says David, wearing a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the LORD. All his might, friends. If I danced with all my might, my mustache would knock my own hat off.

The answer is that she despises him. Verse 16 says Michal, Saul's daughter, looked down from a window, saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, and she despised him in her heart. The text puts it in her heart, so the contempt is quiet for now. Her words come later.

The answer is blessed. Verse 18 says that when David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts. He wasn't done after the offerings. He sent the people off with a blessing.

The answer is False. When David goes home to bless his household, Michal, Saul's daughter, comes out to meet him. Verse 20 has her say, “How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today!” Then she says he uncovered himself in the sight of the maidservants, like a vulgar person would do. She doesn't praise how he honored the LORD.

The answer is that he uncovered himself like a vulgar person. Michal says, “He has uncovered himself today in the sight of the maidservants of his subjects, like a vulgar person would do.” Those are her words from verse 20. They're sharp, and I think they're meant to sting.

The answer is father. David says the LORD “…chose me over your father and all his house…” (verse 21). Michal is Saul's daughter, so he's speaking straight to her. David says the LORD appointed him ruler over His people Israel.

The answer is that he'll celebrate and humble himself even more. David says, “I will celebrate before the LORD, and I will humiliate and humble myself even more than this.” Michal's words didn't slow him down, friends. He says he'll go even further.
